title: Sweet Cheese Dumplings with Sour Cream and Berries
changes_from_base: Same sour-cream dough, shaping and boiling; the filling is smooth sieved farmer's cheese sweetened with sugar, vanilla and lemon zest and bound with an egg yolk (heated to 71 °C in the boil); served sweet with melted butter, icing sugar, sour cream and berries instead of fried onions and chives.
summary: This follows the classic potato-cheese pierogi method for the dough, shaping and boiling, but the filling is smooth sweetened farmer's cheese with vanilla and lemon, bound with egg yolk and heated to 71°C in the boil. They are served with melted butter, icing sugar, sour cream and fresh berries instead of onions and chives.
equipment: 7.5 cm round cutter or a glass
2 trays and a clean tea towel

ingredients.item: plain flour, plus extra for dusting
fine sea salt or table salt
cold water (up to 4 tbsp if needed)
farmer's cheese (twaróg) or well-drained cottage cheese

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: This sweet version uses the same dough, shaping and boiling as the classic potato-cheese pierogi. Whisk the flour and dough salt in the large bowl, mix in the egg with a fork until clumpy, then work in the sour cream and soft butter with your fingertips to a rough, slightly sticky ball, adding water 1 tbsp at a time only if dry flour remains. Knead for 3-4 min on a lightly floured surface until smooth, then wrap and rest for 30 min at room temperature (or up to 24 h in the fridge, with 20 min back at room temperature before rolling). The rest lets the gluten relax so the dough rolls thinly.

steps.title: Prepare the cheese
steps.text: If using cottage cheese, drain it in the sieve for 20 min and press out the liquid. Push the cheese through the sieve or ricer into the medium bowl until smooth and lump-free. Excess moisture would make the filling runny and weaken the seal.

steps.title: Sweeten the filling
steps.text: Beat in the sugar, egg yolk, vanilla and lemon zest until the mixture is thick enough to hold its shape on a spoon. Cover and chill until needed, up to 24 h; cold filling is firmer and easier to wrap.

steps.title: Shape the pierogi
steps.text: Halve the dough, keeping one half wrapped, and roll the other on a lightly floured surface to 2 mm thick. Cut 7.5 cm rounds, add a level tablespoon (about 13 g) of filling to each, fold into a half-moon and pinch firmly from end to end, pressing out any air; crimp with a fork if you like. Set on a floured tray under a tea towel, reroll the scraps once after a 5 min rest and repeat with the second half to make about 40, using up all the filling.

steps.title: Boil and check
steps.text: Bring a large pan of unsalted water to a rolling boil, lower in 10-12 pierogi at a time and stir gently once. When they float, cook for 3 min more so the filling, which contains raw egg yolk, heats right through. Cut one open and check with the probe that the filling reads 71°C before lifting the batch out.

steps.title: Butter and serve
steps.text: Lift the pierogi with the slotted spoon onto a tray brushed with some of the melted butter, which stops them sticking together. Brush the hot pierogi with the rest of the butter, dust with icing sugar and serve about 10 per person with sour cream and berries.

tips: Press the cheese through a sieve for a silky filling; lumps of curd can poke through the thin dough.
Drain cottage cheese well, as watery filling leaks during boiling.
Dust with icing sugar just before serving so it does not dissolve on the hot butter.
safety: A common mistake is skipping the probe check; the filling contains raw egg yolk, so always confirm it reaches 71°C.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Cool within 2 hours, refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat by pan-frying in a little butter until piping hot (74°C). Freeze uncooked pierogi on a tray, then bag, for up to 3 months; boil from frozen, adding 2-3 min and checking the filling reaches 71°C.
